307.report:
Independent review of PR #307, three rounds, head e19078b (earlier rounds 57d5440 and cce4117), base stage. The reviewer ran in a separate context and never edited the implementation.

ROUND 1 (57d5440). Product side clean: no references to any removed name anywhere in *.py/*.iss/*.spec/*.ps1/*.bat, verified both by grep and by an AST scan of SetupWizard for attributes that are read but never assigned. Step indices confirmed: STEPS and renderers line up one to one, LAST=5, the Finish gate moved correctly from step 5 to step 4, and only the Multilogin gate was lost, which was the point. Re-running setup on a configured machine was verified live rather than by test: a .env seeded with MULTILOGIN_AUTOMATION_TOKEN_A in both quoted and exported forms survived two calls to apply_machine_configuration; mutations that put the key back into env_values, or made merge_env drop unknown keys, both went red. The build is untouched: acl_windows.spec never listed a removed name, and the wizard no longer imports src.web at all.

One real defect: test_setup_is_six_steps_and_the_screens_match_them promised to match the step list against the renderer list but asserted block.count("self._") == len(STEPS), which is a count. Swapping self._identity with self._files left the suite green — the wizard would have shown "Your name" above the file pickers and parsed the stats workbook on the wrong step, silently.

Two notes: the Readiness list showed four green ticks and read as "all done" with the Multilogin warning as a separate paragraph below; and Finish said "press Connect" while the Accounts screen carries three buttons containing that word, the right one being "Connect Multilogin".

ROUND 2 (cce4117). The counting test now compares names in order. Eight ways of desynchronising the two lists were tried — removing an element, adding one, swapping non-adjacent pairs, reordering STEPS against renderers, reordering both consistently, a cyclic shift, and duplicating a renderer — all red. The button name is fixed and matches _account_map_add.html line 70.

New blind spots found in the replacement test: it read the source as text, so commenting the line out left it green over an empty screen (the neighbouring phrase test had the same illness), and it did not check colour at all, so turning the yellow marker green passed. A four-line stand was demonstrated: _readiness runs without Tk given system_checks, configuration, stats_path, creatives_path and a stubbed _text.

ROUND 3 (e19078b). Both blind spots closed. The _draw stand was compared against a real tkinter render under root.withdraw(): Readiness matched 10 widgets to 10 rows with identical text, colour and order; Finish matched all three labels, the stand simply not seeing the Button. Commenting out either phrase, turning the marker green, replacing the bullet with a tick, deleting the row, moving it above the checks, and putting the green Safety line back under the yellow one all go red.

Two tails, both non-blocking and both recorded as follow-up work. The adjacency assertion names one specific line at one specific offset: a different green line directly below, or the Safety line one row further down, still pass. And the stand cannot see the Tk Button on Finish — a typo in a Tk option (text= written as txet=) raises TclError in a real render but leaves the suite green; this was equally true before this change, so it is an open gap rather than a regression.

Test runs, all three rounds: 196 passed, 1 skipped, and one pre-existing unrelated failure in tests/test_team_library.py, which is ACL-1289 (tests reach into the real target library) and floats between tests of that file between runs.

Verdict: e19078b may be merged into stage.

ROUND 4 (f7476f2). The tracker refused to record the approval of e19078b because the working branch was two commits behind main; both were merges of this branch own earlier PR (#304 into stage, then stage into main via #306). Current main was merged into the branch. The merge is purely procedural and was verified as such rather than assumed: the tree SHA of f7476f2 is identical to the tree SHA of e19078b (6024920a), so git diff between the two heads is empty and the working tree did not change by a single byte. main is now an ancestor of the head. The one real risk of such a merge was checked explicitly: tests/test_the_installer_signs_in_to_multilogin.py still exists in main and this branch deletes it, so the merge could have resurrected it; it did not, the deletion survived and still stands in the diff against main. Nothing foreign arrived: everything main touched under packaging/windows since the branch base was this same task four commits. Test runs repeat the approved head exactly. The approval of e19078b therefore carries over to f7476f2 without reservation.

Independent review of PR #312 (ACL-1311 Team access), three rounds; the reviewer ran in a separate context and never edited the implementation. Head e95ef60, base stage 723652e.

ROUND 1 (9505d6e). Approved, no blocking findings. Security of the token route verified through ASGI: GET/HEAD/OPTIONS 405, Origin null 403, cross-site Referer 403, Origin localhost other port + Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site 403, foreign Host (evil.example, localhost.evil.example, 127.0.0.1.nip.io) 400 — none return the token. A local process without Origin gets it, which is not new: it can read the machine .env anyway. No token in logs at DEBUG, Sentry has send_default_pii=False, token never lands in markup or DOM, including the real Clipboard API branch checked on http://127.0.0.1. sign_in is called only from /multilogin-signin; the leftover builder panel is dead code and hits the server refusal. A dead token never shows as connected. Findings: the setup wizard still told buyers to sign in with email and password; 11 of 32 mutations survived, the real gaps being copy from the wrong slot, next_step for expired, Copy on a dead token, false 'copied' when execCommand fails, flag case, the +60 s margin, 401 without exp called expired; a refused Clipboard API showed a raw browser error; deployment notes missing (restart after setting the flag, flag absent from .env.example).

ROUND 2 (a5ee726). All seven author mutations red, none passing by coincidence; the clipboard fallback on 127.0.0.1 works after a refused writeText with and without permissions; packaging/windows/tests 45 OK. Four remaining non-blocking gaps: the fallback after a refused Clipboard API was not exercised because the test page ran on http://acl.test (no secure context); the 'not accepted' label untested; a dead 'expired if readable' branch; the Readiness wizard text untested.

ROUND 3 (e95ef60). All four closed. The new test runs the page on http://127.0.0.1:9 (isSecureContext true) with a refused writeText; removing the fallback or replacing it with an empty catch turns it red. 8 of 9 delta mutations red; the survivor (always copying through the field) is not a gap, copying still works. 338.report: Approved. The change to _discover_owned_debug_port.norm (src/fb_ads_rpa/browser.py:1542-1554) is correct and fixes the root cause of the 2026-09-27 stage incident. On this machine (Python 3.14.3), os.path.realpath of a real GetShortPathNameW name in a temp dir returns the long path, identical to realpath of the long form. A missing tail under a short prefix still expands the existing prefix. A junction resolves to its target, so the same profile can't look like two different ones, and two different directories can't collapse into one. Quotes are stripped before realpath. Live psutil on this machine shows every Mimic --user-data-dir fully in 8.3 form (C:\Users\EVGENI~1\mlx\profiles\B18D03~1\3EF7F4~1\5D508A~1). The stage log confirms the chain: at 08:45 the profiles were reattached, but ownership failed on the path compare, so _mark_robot_profile was never called. At 12:33 connect_over_cdp timed out and _robot_profile returned False, so the job stopped with no_automation_port (browser.py:2076-2080). The earlier 1443 unowned_port stop at 08:45:47 has the same cause (browser.py:2062-2065). The hand-opened-profile protection is unchanged: a process still has to own a LISTEN socket on its debug port and accept CDP. The new test file, plus the hand-opened, spend-regression and two-minute suites, pass: 67 passed in a detached worktree. Both short-path tests fail against base 47152af, so they do guard the regression. Non-blocking notes: (1) Four substring helpers build needles from the long path and its leaf, and those needles never match 8.3 command lines: _kill_chrome_for_user_data_dir (browser.py:145-184), _profile_process_running (1450-1476), _discover_debug_port (1478-1531) and _profile_pids (1840-1866). They still work only because the main Mimic process carries the profile id in --client-session-id (4/4 live main processes). That is an undocumented MLX detail, so a realpath-based compare there would be sturdier. (2) After this fix, a robot profile whose CDP connect times out now goes to _start_via_mlx_api (browser.py:2090). That may return the same hung port, so the live acceptance criterion should be checked on a real run. (3) realpath costs about 1 ms per call here, roughly 40 ms per check across 38 Mimic processes. That is acceptable, and a raw-string equality short-circuit or cache would remove it. The except fallback is effectively dead. For an unreachable UNC path, realpath returned instantly with an odd C:\host\... result, which is harmless because profiles are local. (4) account_spend._dir_spellings (src/analysis_agent/account_spend.py:525) is now a redundant workaround; dashboard track can simplify it later. Follow-up: the only change after the reviewed head 2d1a42d is a merge of work/main (19fadc3); the tree is byte-identical (f4d92c5361dcf21dbc9b2c4fc18cb32fe508360e), so the approval carries over unchanged.

343.report: Round 3 re-review in a fresh detached worktree (C:/acl-rev343c, removed after review). All 8 PR test files pass one at a time (symlink tests skip x2+2 for lack of privilege): meta_campaign_agent 7+2skip, account-header 2, asset-export 6, click-recorder 5, creative-file 4+2skip, dead-multilogin-panel 6, scrubber-shapes 50, scrubber-never-hangs 16. acl_scan_secrets.py: clean. THE ROUND-2 BLOCKER IS FIXED: the quoted-value pattern is now (?:\\.|(?!\4)[^\\\n])* with an optional closing quote group (\4)?. Independently fuzzed every regex in run_telemetry.py (scrub/_SCRUB alternatives and scrub_diag/_hides_dict_value) via subprocess-isolated adversarial inputs: unterminated quotes with 28..50000 backslash pairs, truncated JSON-escaped Windows paths, FB-style escaped-slash HTML fragments, 100KB and 4MB (the real MAX_HTML_BYTES ceiling) unterminated payloads, long runs of hyphen/dot/space/camelCase-hump separators (up to 50000 reps), 2000-5000 keys in one blob, and a 100KB random adversarial mix. All completed in well under the test suite's own 0.5s/case ceiling; the 4MB worst case (realistic page_capture.scrub_html ceiling) took 1.8s, linear. Mutation-tested: (a) reintroducing the exact round-2-flagged ambiguous alternation (?:\\.|(?!\4).)* alone did NOT reintroduce the blowup, because the newly-added optional closing-quote group means the overall match can never fail at that position, so the engine never backtracks into the ambiguous alternation regardless of exclusivity -- informational only, not a defect, the shipped pattern keeps both defenses; (b) narrowing _KEY_SEP back to '_?' correctly broke 6 of the round-2 hyphen/dot/space/header tests, confirming that fix is real and covered. S01 dead-panel JS: no remaining raw cid/instance concatenation into onclick/oninput JS text or unescaped id/CSS-selector attributes in that block; the two round-2-flagged spots (oninput filters at old report.html:8548/8681) now pass cid via data-cid+this.dataset, ids go through aclEscHtml, and the two querySelector call sites use CSS.escape(cid); the two getElementById/.id-property sites that still string-concat cid are safe (DOM property/exact-id-lookup, not markup or eval'd JS text). NON-BLOCKING (new, previously unflagged): (1) the round-2 suffix-matching widening of _BARE_KEY_START to treat '_' as a valid boundary (not just non-word chars) means the STRING-based scrub() -- unlike the dict-based scrub_diag/_hides_dict_value, which is deliberately bool/int/None-aware and is tested for this -- has no way to tell a boolean/counter flag from a real secret, so free text like 'has_token: True', 'hasToken: true', 'is_token=False' gets redacted to 'has_token: <hidden>' etc; this reaches Sentry/telemetry whenever such text appears inside a diag string value (verified: scrub_diag({'note': 'has_token: True, alive: False'}) hides the flag). Loses diagnostic value, does not leak a secret. The code's own comment and test only promise this stays visible for actual dict keys. (2) the quoted-key form's prefix is bounded to 40 lazy characters (by design, for linear time); a key whose junk/organization-specific prefix before the recognized secret suffix exceeds ~40-46 chars is NOT redacted at all -- e.g. '{"' + 'x'*45 + '_refresh_token":"SECRET"}' leaks the value in full. Narrow/contrived in practice (no such key names exist in this codebase today) but a real false negative if it ever occurs; worth a comment noting the tradeoff or raising the bound modestly. Neither blocks: no realistic new secret-leak path was found, the intended threat model (real credential field names in this codebase and common header spellings) is covered, and the P1 ReDoS is conclusively closed. | Coordinator note: head moved bde9473->768df3a by a merge of work/main only; tree unchanged (889bc37), verified with git rev-parse HEAD^{tree} before and after.

Runs f9b9fc8d7bb3, 8ce1b9985046 and b3a333ff43ab, Facebook_1443, simple_create:

By about 13 s the dialog had closed by itself, a second Ad row "New Leads Ad" was in the tree, and the ad section showed that new empty ad (name "New Leads Ad", "Set up creative", empty Website URL).
- The dialog's text was never captured. It was most likely Meta's creation progress modal. It is now recorded in `diag.dialog`.

## Implemented
- `simple_create.create_next_ad`:
  - Presses Action menu → Create ad. Presses are guarded; never Duplicate/Delete/default/Publish/footer, never Escape.
  - Waits up to 30 s for three things: a new Ad row, the ad section showing an ad whose name is not already built, and the dialog closing.
  - Failure reasons are named. A page capture is taken only on failure. Menu labels are logged without object ids (step 1 had leaked an ad set id into telemetry labels).
- In the flow, ads 2+ in simple_create use the same per-ad fill as the classic path. After that, `simple_create.ad_listed` checks the name in the ad list; the editor is never reopened.
- While ads 2+ are filled, `_reloads_blocked` refuses every reload path: `recover_stuck_page`, `_reload_editor`, the copy-reveal reload, the upload stalled retry (`reload=False`) and the overlays (`may_reload=False`). Each refusal is logged as `loading_modal_reload` with ok=False and note `refused:simple_create_new_ad`.
- After a failed create, the remaining ads get `adN_create:not_tried`. The final destination recheck applies only to the open ad.
- `simple_create_more_ads` now only means switched off (`FB_RPA_SIMPLE_MORE_ADS_PRESS=0`).

- `tests/test_simple_create_more_ads.py`: 12 tests on the new fixture. They replace `test_simple_create_more_ads_capture.py`.

- **Busy-wait design:**
  - `is_progress_dialog` recognises the dialog by its surface (`ads_progress_dialog`) or its text (Creating... / Creando / Loading creation).
  - In `_wait_new_ad`, an unanswered read whose last answered read showed the progress dialog starts a busy window: `busy_since` is set, and the wait probes about once a second with no presses or reloads, inside `hold_open_ad`.   - The deadline becomes max(start + 30 s, `busy_since` + `META_BUSY_WAIT_S`), with `META_BUSY_WAIT_S` = 120 s.
  - The wait ends normally once the new row, the stable new name and no dialog are all there.
  - If the page is still unanswered at `busy_since` + 120 s, the result is `tab_frozen` with `busy_s`. The reason names the silence and the limit, and says the empty new ad may still appear.
  - A closed tab is never waited for. Silence without the progress dialog is `tab_frozen` at once, as before.
  - `busy_s` goes on the existing `simple_create_more_ads` step; there are no new step names.

# ACL-1388 handoff (Worker-H1388D)

PR #396 into stage, head 7f3b50ce3b9ebdced27288a7821d0fbead4a2ac6 (contains work/main ef174b9).

## Scope

A Multilogin window opened by hand no longer always stops the account with `profile_open_by_hand`. When publishing, the robot closes it and reopens it with automation, but only when it is safe (owner decision, Issue #388).

- New `src/fb_ads_rpa/hand_window.py` runs the safety check. All of these must hold:
  1. the profile's browser has been running for at least `MIN_AGE_S` = 15 min. The age is `now - create_time` of the **youngest** main Mimic process found by `_profile_pids`.
  2. the foreground window does not belong to the profile. It checks `GetForegroundWindow` and `GetWindowThreadProcessId`, and treats a match on the profile's own pid or any parent pid as "in the foreground". If there is no foreground window at all (locked screen), the check counts as passed.
  3. the machine has had no keyboard or mouse input for at least `MIN_IDLE_S` = 60 s, read with `GetLastInputInfo`/`GetTickCount` using 32-bit wrap math.
  If the process can't be found, the machine isn't Windows, or any psutil or Win32 read fails, the result is "not safe" and today's stop applies.
  Each machine can override the thresholds with `FB_RPA_HAND_WINDOW_MIN_AGE_S` and `FB_RPA_HAND_WINDOW_MIN_IDLE_S`. `FB_RPA_REOPEN_HAND_WINDOW=0` turns the feature off and restores the old always-stop behaviour.
- In `browser.py`, `MultiloginAttachOnlyProvider._reopen_hand_opened` is used at all three places a hand-opened window is detected: `no_automation_port`, `unowned_port`, and `mlx_lock` (the last one caught around `_start_via_mlx_api` in `open()`). It runs only when `allow_restart and allow_kill`, which means publishing. Spend reading passes `allow_kill=False` and still stops as before.
  - If the check fails, the account stops with the same `profile_open_by_hand` code, message and detail as before, and nothing is touched.
  - If the check passes, the robot calls `_stop_profile(..., allow_kill=False)`, which is the MLX API stop of this profile only. If the API stop fails, nothing is killed and the old stop applies. The robot then waits up to 20 s for the hand-opened processes to exit; if they are still running, the old stop applies and nothing is started. After that it runs `_start_via_mlx_api(allow_kill=False)` and connects. A failure after the window was closed is reported as `profile_restart_failed`.
  - The login check stays where it already is: the way to the campaigns list stops a logged-out profile with `profile_logged_out`. The reopen happens once per attach and there is no retry loop.
- The change is visible in three places:
  - a job panel line, "Closed the hand-opened window of <account> and reopened it for the robot". It goes through the existing job notice channel (`creative_compress.report_notice`, the one already rendered from `creative_notices`), so the template is unchanged.
  - a telemetry row `profile_hand_window` with `note` = outcome or refusal reason and `diag` = where, workspace, reason, age_s and idle_s. It carries no profile id. `profile_` steps already map to the "hold" stage in the progress model.
  - a Sentry breadcrumb (`category=profile`) with the same data.
- `tests/conftest.py` adds an autouse fixture that sets `FB_RPA_REOPEN_HAND_WINDOW=0`, so no test reads the live machine's windows or input. The ACL-1388 tests turn it back on.
- There is a new entry in `docs/system/CHANGELOG.md`.

## Checks

- New `tests/test_a_hand_opened_profile_is_reopened_when_safe.py` (32 tests), with the Win32, psutil and MLX layers stubbed. It covers the happy path (API stop, then start, then connect, with no kill), each gate (young window, youngest process decides, foreground, foreground child process, recent input), failed reads (age, foreground, parent chain, idle), no process, not Windows, env overrides, the off switch, a failed MLX stop, a window still running after the stop, a failed start after the close, the `unowned_port` and `mlx_lock` paths, spend reading never closing a window, and robot-started profiles skipping the check. Two more cases:
  - a publisher-level test where the reopened profile is logged out: the result is `profile_logged_out`, with one stop and one start, and the second campaign doesn't touch the browser;
  - a smoke test of the real ctypes layer on Windows.
- The existing ACL-1320 tests in `test_a_hand_opened_profile_is_never_stopped.py` still pass unchanged.
- Full suite on the final head (the branch contains `work/main` ef174b9): 3837 passed, 6 skipped, 1 failed (the known flake `test_campaign_build_percent_browser.py::test_the_percent_sits_next_to_the_dot_and_keeps_the_tooltip`, passes on rerun alone), 56m41s, empty `ACL_LIBRARY_*`.

## Risks

- **Foreground detection:** Chrome's top-level window belongs to the main browser process. If Mimic ever puts it in a process outside the parent chain, the foreground check would miss it. The idle-input gate still has to pass, so someone actively working always blocks the close.
- **No foreground window:** a locked screen (no foreground window) counts as "not the profile", which is the intended unattended case.
- **Not live-checked yet:** acceptance item 5 (open a profile by hand, leave it idle past the threshold, press Publish) still needs a live run.
- **Rollback:** set `FB_RPA_REOPEN_HAND_WINDOW=0` on the machine.

Where the cold time went, per the profile: `config/analysis_rules.py:_load_raw` was called 60 256 times and took 69 of the 106 s. `normalize_text_segment` read the rules JSON with `open` + `is_file` for every workbook row. The next cost was `_log_unknown_interests` at about 15 s: for each unknown code it rescanned the whole workbook and re-read the journal. What remains is openpyxl reading the workbook and the report assembly.

### What changed
- **Load once:** `analysis_rules` parses the file once and re-checks it against disk (mtime + size) at most every 2 s, so a hand edit still takes effect without a restart. Callers get a copy. The unknown-interest log now runs in one pass (`logged_unknown_targets()` is read once). The numbers shown do not change.
- **Report off the loop:**
  - `GET /` on a cold cache returns `loading.html` ("Loading the numbers…") straight away and starts a background build of the report and that page's period.
  - The loading page polls `/report/status` and reloads itself when the report is ready.
  - If the build fails, the next load renders the normal error page.
  - Builds are single-flight (`_BUILD_LOCK`), so page fragments wait for the one build instead of each starting their own. `force_rebuild` reuses a result only when that build started after the request.
  - The cache entry is published with its key set last.
  - Every handler that reads the report runs in its own `_REPORT_POOL`, so waiters never take threads that cancel or publish need. These handlers are `/details`, `/export/assets`, `/brief`, `/api/creatives`, `/api/buyers` (GET and POST), `/api/accounts-overview`, `/account-spend/countries`, `/account-map`, `/account-map/available`, `/account-links` unlink and `/build-upload` renders.
  - Preview and publish start build their drafts in a thread.
  - `/acl/update/check` runs `git fetch` (timeout up to 120 s) in a thread.
  - `/health` waits at most 0.3 s for the git-based version. Startup pre-warms the version and the first slots snapshot, which imports psutil.
- **Stop:** `cancel_job` runs `publisher.cancel()` in its own short-lived thread (see cause 1 below).
- **Publish is never lost silently:**
  - Each submission carries a `request_id`. `start_job` holds a lock per key and returns the job it already created for a repeated key (ACL-1355 duplicate guards unchanged).
  - The page treats a network failure, a non-JSON answer or no answer within 45 s as "server busy". The account panel and the drawer show "The dashboard server is busy and did not answer — nothing was sent twice" with a **Retry** button.
  - Retry resends with the same key. The account stays busy until then, so Publish / Publish all cannot send a second job past it.
  - This replaces the old "Submission outcome unknown — reload (F5)" freeze for network failures.

### Hang causes (from the live logs; times in the logs are local, UTC+3)
1. **2026-09-29 12:54:59 local (09:54:59 UTC), `C:\acl-live-0928`, build f036583.** The log fills with `loop <ProactorEventLoop running=True> is not the running loop`, `There is no current event loop in thread 'MainThread'` and anyio `no running event loop`, then the server stops answering and is restarted at 13:08.
   - Mechanism: `POST /publish-jobs/{id}/cancel` → `cancel_job` → `RpaPublisher.cancel()` → `BrowserConnection.close()` ran **on the event-loop thread**. That calls the job thread's sync Playwright (`playwright.stop()` from a foreign thread) and then `browser._reset_asyncio_running_loop()`, which clears the *calling* thread's running-loop mark.
   - I reproduced the exact error text by calling `_reset_asyncio_running_loop()` inside a running loop.
   - The job's telemetry stops at 09:54:38 UTC and the loop breaks 21 s later. The cancel's own access-log line is missing because the handler never completed.
   - The `[RPA] Human takeover timed out` print next to it is stdout, which is buffered, so its position in the log is not reliable.
   - Fixed here: cancel never runs the RPA teardown on the loop thread (test with a fake publisher that does exactly that).
2. **2026-09-30 ~12:00–12:06 UTC, `C:\acl-live-0928`, build 354d610.**
   - At 14:59:41 local, three jobs got `TargetClosedError`. The three cancels at about 12:00–12:02 UTC returned 200, and the server kept answering for a while.
   - Then came `POST /refresh`, `GET /?date_from=2026-09-29…` and `/acl/update/check`, and after that nothing more was logged until the kill (the log mtime is 15:06 local). There are no asyncio errors this time, so the loop was blocked, not broken.

### Out of scope (RPA track)

After this PR that is a throwaway thread, but the proper fix is for the job thread to disconnect itself. `src/fb_ads_rpa/**` is not changed here.

# Review of PR #446 [ACL-1444]: auto-close clean profiles, "Close profile" button

- Reviewer: Reviewer-R1444C (rev_r1444c_1001). Implementer: Worker-Z1444Y
- Head 39f40e0a5f69a15abf1f4e0ec5de14ad63885947, base work/stage 3a629ca36796243ef04d90dcd9c120bf101de17a, tree 81016dc83af3c4483096b67ec22f7a943927b7d8
- **Verdict: request-changes**

## Blocking

**F1 (High): the draft-saved check is skipped on Meta's current single-screen editor.** At `src/fb_ads_rpa/rpa_publisher.py` `_draft_saved`, the check is `meta_dom._on_editor(page)`, and that function is just `"/edit" in page.url` (`meta_dom.py:3571`). The production editor since ACL-1327 is `/adsmanager/manage/simple_create`, which has no "/edit" in the URL. The editor the Issue names ("single-screen editor shows All edits saved") is therefore treated as "not in the editor, nothing unsaved". `_draft_saved` returns True without waiting for autosave or seeing "All edits saved", and the profile gets stopped.
  - Reproduced: with `_all_edits_saved` set to False and the URL `.../adsmanager/manage/simple_create?act=1`, `RpaPublisher._draft_saved` returns **True**.
  - The codebase already has the right predicate: `meta_dom._ad_editor_url(url)` (`"/ads/edit/" in url or url_is_simple_create(url)`, meta_dom.py:14315). Use that, or `"/edit" in url or url_is_simple_create(url)`. Better still, fail closed and treat any URL that is not the campaign list as "must see All edits saved".
  - The test `test_the_editor_must_say_all_edits_saved` only uses `/campaigns/edit` and `/campaigns` URLs. Add a simple_create case.

## Non-blocking

- **F2 (Low): cancel race.** In `rpa_publisher.py` `finish_job`, `self._cancelled` is read once, before `_draft_saved`, which can wait up to about 16.5 s. A Stop pressed during that wait still lets the profile close. In practice `cancel()` drops CDP and `_draft_saved` then raises, which gives kept_unsaved, so the window is small. Re-check `self._cancelled` right before `close_finished_profile`.
- **F3 (Low): unscrubbed error in a log.** `rpa_publisher.py` `finish_job` uses `log.warning("...closing the finished profile failed: %s", account_label, exc)` with the raw exception. Use `_exc_text`/`scrub`, as browser.py and `close_profile` already do. User-facing texts are fixed strings, and telemetry carries only the provider name.
- **F4 (Low): early slot wake.** `publish_jobs.py` `_let_go_of_profile` calls `_slots.wake()` while the job still holds its slot. `_slots.release` in `_run_job`'s finally notifies again moments later, so this is harmless but redundant. The button path's wake is correct.
- **F5 (Low): "for this job" is wider than the job.** `_ROBOT_PROFILES` covers the whole process lifetime, not this job. A profile the robot attached in an earlier job (same process still running) counts as the robot's. The same-pid check keeps hand-reopened windows safe. `_robot_profile` also returns True when pids cannot be read (inherited ACL-1320 semantics). Acceptable; noting it only.
- **F6 (Low): close then immediate reopen.** If another job on the same profile is already queued (two labels, one profile), auto-close stops the profile and the next job reopens it right away. Safe but wasteful. Consider skipping the close when an active job with the same `profile_key_for` exists.
- **F7 (Info): button UX.** The button shows on every finished panel, including stale ones, while another job on that profile runs. The server answers 409 with an English message, so the Issue's "disabled while running" holds server-side only. The button also closes hand-opened windows on purpose (human request, graceful API stop, no kill). That is fine, but the hint text could say so.

# Review of PR #449 [ACL-1445]: independent review by Reviewer-R1445D

Head 324c9ba0bfaa1d34704199d573b7356a479c7a00 · base work/stage 3a629ca36796243ef04d90dcd9c120bf101de17a · tree 4a375392da7afbceeabb81472063c82a5908c6a5
Implementer: Worker-L1445P. Session: rev_r1445d_1001.

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The single-screen anchor and the loading wait are sound and fail closed. The "not offered" rule and the summary read-back can each let a campaign pass while a placement that should be OFF is still ON. A scratch probe (not committed) shows two of these false passes in the bench emulation.

## Findings

### B1 (blocker): the tail of a virtualised category becomes "not offered" and the step passes with those placements ON
src/fb_ads_rpa/meta_dom.py:8221-8277 (`_settle_category`), 8362-8380.
The rule treats a category as complete when all three of these hold:
- the visible labels have not changed for 1.5 s;
- some of the category's own rows are rendered;
- every ON row was rendered.

None of these shows that the list was rendered to its end. In Feeds both ON rows (Facebook Feed, Instagram feed) come first and all 8 OFF rows follow, so a tail that is not mounted is still judged complete. 8e9acb2 (ACL-1220, 17.09 CO_bnc FX) recorded exactly this live: "Threads feed" and "Facebook Notifications" were not in the DOM until the list was scrolled. `_settle_category` never scrolls. The only scroll before it is the earlier wheel loop: 3 x 400 px wheel ticks while hovering, which breaks on `subitems_scroll_error`, and nothing checks that the region's end was reached. A stable, half-rendered list therefore passes.

Probe: the Doc19 bench with "Threads feed" and "Facebook Notifications" hidden from the reader (`offsetParent === null`, the same as unmounted for `_subitem_labels`). Result: `fill_placements` returned True, `subitems_missing` was [] and `subitems_not_offered` was ["Threads feed", "Facebook Notifications", "Messenger Stories"]. Both rows were still checked=True.

Fix: before calling anything "not offered", scroll the open category's region to its end, read again, and require proof of the end. For example, the region's last row is followed in view by the next category button ("Search results"), or the scroll container is at its bottom. Add a bench test with a tail that mounts only after scrolling, and one where the tail never mounts. The first must set the rows OFF and the second must fail.

### B2 (high): an item called "not offered" in its mapped category hides a later failure to switch it off
src/fb_ads_rpa/meta_dom.py:8370-8380.
`not_offered` is filtered against `subitems_seen` only when that category is checked. If the row then appears in a later category and cannot be switched off, it stays in `remaining_off`. The final line `offered_off = [x for x in remaining_off if x not in not_offered]` then drops it from `subitems_missing`. The row can appear later because Meta moved it, or because the mapping is wrong. The switch-off can fail because the row is locked, or because a click failed after a re-collapse.

Probe: "Messenger Stories" absent from Stories, present in In-stream, checked and disabled. Result: `fill_placements` returned True, `subitems_not_offered` was ["Messenger Stories"], and the row was seen and is still checked=True.

Fix: at the end, keep only the not-offered items that never appear in `report["subitems_seen"]`. Any item that was seen and is still in `remaining_off` is a failure.

### B3 (high): the summary read-back accepts any 7 included placements
src/fb_ads_rpa/meta_dom.py:8071-8093 (`_placements_summary` at 6798-6831).
The check is `included == len(_SUBITEMS_ON)` (not a literal 7, which is good), `limited == 0` and `excluded > 0`. The counts cannot tell which 7 placements are included. Suppose 6 wanted ON rows are on, 1 wanted ON row is off, and an OFF row such as Messenger Stories or a Search results item is still on. That still shows "Included: 7".

This is a realistic path, not a hypothetical one. `run_recorded_campaign_flow` (meta_dom.py:5768-5773) retries `fill_placements` after `recover_stuck_page`. A partial first attempt that failed on exactly such a swap would be accepted on the retry from the collapsed summary, without anything being read back.

The path was also not asked for in Issue #445: it is scope creep. Its fixture was rebuilt from screenshot text, not from a capture. The negative test only checks Included: 21.

Fix, in order of preference:
1. Drop the path and keep the old failure.
2. Expand the summary and read back the rows.
3. Accept a summary only when this same `fill_placements` call has already confirmed every ON row and every offered OFF row. That never happens in the retry case.

If the path stays, add a test where the same counts hide a wrong set.

### M1 (medium): the tests do not cover the core risk
tests/test_bench_placements.py.
`test_an_unrendered_list_is_not_a_false_not_offered` hides every row of Stories, which the ON-rows check catches trivially. No test hides only an OFF tail (B1), and none sees an item in another category (B2). The late-row test uses a 1 s delay, inside the 1.5 s quiet window, so it does not exercise a row arriving after the list has settled.

The xfail-to-pass, Doc19, loading and loaded-card tests are real. They run the real `fill_placements` in offline headless Chromium against capture fragments.

### L1 (low): the single-screen card is not re-tagged after it loads
src/fb_ads_rpa/meta_dom.py:7454-7477.
After `_wait_placements_section_loaded` the marker is not re-applied. If React remounts the section, readers fall back to `document` (for example `_categories_visible` and `_subitem_labels`). That fails closed or reads outside the card. Re-run `_tag_placements_section` (or the primary tag) once the card has loaded.

`sectionLoading` relies on `role=progressbar` with aria-busy or aria-valuetext. A spinner without those attributes means no wait, and the step later fails as "categories not visible" rather than `placements_card_loading`. That fails closed, so it is acceptable.

### L2 (low): the categories check uses a minimum count
"All categories present" means `seen >= 5` over `_PLACEMENT_CATEGORIES`. Doc19's new 6th category, "Marketing messages", is not managed. In the capture it is disabled and unchecked, so there is no risk today. Worth a note.

## Checked and OK
- `_SUBITEMS_BY_CATEGORY` matches the live Doc19 `subitems_seen` grouping, and the test asserts it covers ON+OFF and the wanted categories exactly. ON items are never "not offered". `on_unseen` uses the cumulative `here`, so rows unmounted while scrolling do not block completion. That is correct for ON rows, and it is the B1 risk for OFF rows.
- Single-screen anchor `[data-surface$="adset_placement_static_pgd_section"]` or `#campaignPlacementStaticPGDSection`, restricted to the element that contains the Placements heading. It is used only when the "Account controls" tag fails.
- The 20 s wait is bounded by a monotonic clock and polls every 0.5 s. When the card never loads, the failure is named `placements_card_loading` and the step fails closed.
- Telemetry: `subitems_not_offered` and `verified_by` go to the `after_placements` step row with a note (the `_shot(label, diag, note)` signature matches). `not_offered_check`, `placements_card` and `placements_summary` are in the report and the debug dump.
- The limited-spending JS was extracted to `_LIMITED_SPENDING_OFF_JS` and behaves the same.

## CI
`gh pr checks 392`: all green (test 3.11/3.13, installer, ACL verification, descriptor, tracker-link) — but run on the old base 712fa0c, so it is stale evidence for the merge result.

## Findings
- **B1 (blocking, process) — base not current.** Head does not contain main 91e7049; GitHub reports CONFLICTING. Fix: merge work/main into the branch, resolve CHANGELOG by keeping both entries, push, let CI rerun on the new head.
- **F1 (minor) — account_spend.py:1114–1122 `_blocked_on_page` takes only the first detector hit.** `meta_dom._account_blocked_text` returns the first matching text in DOM order, so on a page with both the "Verification required to advertise" banner and a Delivery "Account disabled" cell (exactly run ecce52f330b8, 22.09) the result is `restricted`, not `disabled`. Fix: in the reader, evaluate `meta_dom._ACCOUNT_BLOCKED_JS` over `meta_dom._roots(page)` itself (still one shared list), map each text via `_account_blocked_match`, add each to `found` so `_STATUS_RANK` decides; add a test with banner + cell → disabled. Cosmetic in the same path: status_text comes out as "...advertiseComplete verification..." (textContent join without space) — acceptable, or use innerText.
- **F2 (minor, pre-existing, follow-up) — unanchored banner phrases.** `meta_dom` "Your ad account is disabled" and `_STATUS_SIGNS` "ad account is disabled" are substring matches; help text like "What to do if your ad account is disabled" reads as `disabled`. Present before this PR (old `_STATUS_SIGNS` page-body match), not a regression. Suggest a follow-up Issue.
- **F3 (low, pre-existing) — English only.** Non-English Ads Manager reads as `clear`. Out of scope for ACL-1391; note in a follow-up if non-English profiles exist.
- **F4 (low) — AC "tests against a saved Ads Manager page (scrubbed)" not met.** Tests use synthetic markup; the live Doc20 read (state=ok, status=disabled, status_text "Account disabled") stands in. Either add a scrubbed capture or get the owner's explicit waiver recorded in the Issue.
- **F5 (low) — "one list" is partial.** Delivery/verification shapes are shared through the import, but the banner list `_STATUS_SIGNS` stays separate and RPA lacks its phrases (e.g. "we restricted your ad account"). The drift test only checks kind→status mapping. Acceptable for this Issue; mention in Handoff.
- **F6 (low) — account_spend.py:1117–1120 silent `except Exception: return None`.** If the RPA private names are renamed, the reader silently falls back to banners-only. Tests would catch it in CI (they import the real meta_dom), so low. Suggest `log.warning` once.
- **N1 (nit)** — `at_short` is "dd.mm" with no year; full timestamp is in the tooltip. Fine.

Checked OK:
- Staleness: last reading per account by `finished_at`; stale only if strictly after status `at` and without a status; running/interrupted readings (empty finished_at) ignored; other accounts ignored. Every ok RPA reading carries a status, so a successful read never marks stale. English tooltip "Not refreshed: the latest read on … failed — <error>." and label "· not refreshed"; autoescaped (Jinja2Templates).
- Map: `disabled`/`restricted`/`blocked` always `amap-st bad` (red), stale `clear` is grey `dim` not `ok`; disabled never renders as "no warning". `--warn` CSS var exists.
- Spend read / turn-off: `_status_once` banner loop unchanged in effect (first state wins via break); detector adds ~1 DOM pass per status try; read_via_rpa, _put, turn-off untouched.
- File ownership: meta_dom.py (RPA) read only, not edited.

Verdict: request-changes
(Required: B1 base update with CI on the new head. Recommended in the same pass: F1 with a test. F2–F6 can be follow-ups.)

## Findings

### F1 — Medium (safety): an ad is taken as "created and open" while the post-Create-ad dialog is still on screen
`src/fb_ads_rpa/simple_create.py:779` (`ready` includes `not dialog`), with the verdict at `:885-897`.
The loop waits for "new row AND new name AND no dialog". But after `wait_s` (30 s) the verdict checks only `ads_after > ads_before` and `name_is_new`. So when the dialog is still open, `ok=True` and the flow goes on to fill ad N under an unknown dialog. It only records `dialog.still_open=True`. This is exactly the review-focus question "what if the unknown dialog waits for input". The next steps are name `_fill`, the creative (`_walk_creative_wizard` / `_close_creative_setup_modal`, which press wizard buttons) and the destination. They would act with an uncaptured modal on top. `_press_allowed` only protects Publish and the footer, not an arbitrary dialog's Continue/Confirm. The implementer lists this as a known risk, but the code does not fail closed.
Mutation proof: dropping `and not got.get("dialog")` from `ready` leaves all 12 tests in `tests/test_simple_create_more_ads.py` green. The condition is untested.
Fix: if the dialog is still open when the wait ends, fail with the named blocking reason `adN_create:dialog_open`, carrying the dialog text/surface in the diag and a page capture, and do not fill. Add a fixture test where the dialog never closes but the row and new name appear.

### F2 — Medium (safety): the copy step can still reopen an ad through the tree while ads 2+ are filled
`src/fb_ads_rpa/meta_dom.py:12563` (`_repair_blocked_copy_editor` → `verify_and_fix_ad_destinations(page, [ad_name], …)` → `_open_tree_ad`) and `:12700` (`_on_the_named_ad` → `_reopen_ad_after_reload` → `_open_tree_ad`).
`_reloads_blocked` stops reloads, but it does not stop tree re-opens. The ad-N copy step is `write_ad_copy(..., ad_name=extra_copy_name)` (`meta_dom.py:~6189`). If a Lead-form review error is visible (`_review_errors_visible`), then `_repair_blocked_copy_editor` clicks the ad's row in the tree. In simple_create that error can be page-wide, for example left over from ad 1. That click is an editor re-open, which the Issue forbids ("never reopen an existing Leads ad editor") and the PR says never happens. `_open_tree_ad` also matches by prefix, taking the leftmost match of any name of 10+ characters that the wanted name starts with. With similar names ("… Ad 2" / "… Ad 3" truncated in the tree), it can click a different, already-built ad. Then `_on_the_named_ad` would open yet another one.
Note: ad 1 in simple mode had the same exposure before this PR (ACL-1327). This PR extends it to ads 2+ and claims the opposite.
Fix: while `_reload_block.why` is set, `_repair_blocked_copy_editor` should call only `_select_browser_addon_none` / `set_ad_destination_website` on the open ad, with no `verify_and_fix_ad_destinations`. `_on_the_named_ad` should return False without `_open_tree_ad`, so the copy fails with a named reason. Add a flow test with `_review_errors_visible=True` for ad 2 that asserts `_open_tree_ad` / `verify_and_fix_ad_destinations` are not called.

### F3 — Low: an empty ad-name field counts as "the new ad is open"
`simple_create.py:754` (`_fresh`). `name_value == ""` is not in `known`, so it counts as fresh. If the ad section re-renders with an empty or not-yet-hydrated name input while the new row is already in the tree, the robot types ad N's name into whatever that section turns out to be.
Fix: require a non-empty value, ideally one that stays the same over two consecutive polls. Or require the "New Leads Ad" pattern, case-insensitive.

### F4 — Low: one reload path is outside the guard
`meta_dom.py:3637/3715`. `_unstick` → `_reload_awake` → `page.reload` does not check `_reload_refused`. On simple_create `_on_editor()` is False (no `/edit` in the URL), so an unresponsive tab under a `_StallWatch` with `reload=True` would reload. Today the `adN_` steps use `reload=False` (`_ADDITIONAL_AD_STEP`), so I found no live route to it. It is still a gap in a guard that claims "no reloads anywhere".
Fix: add `if _reload_refused(page, where): return False` at the top of `_reload_awake`, or in `_unstick` before reloading.

### F5 — Low (tests): the in-function refusals are not unit-tested
The `reload=False` branch in `_upload_ad_creative_with_retry` (`meta_dom.py:9597`), `_clear_blocking_overlays(may_reload=False)` and the `_reveal_ad_copy_fields` refusal are only covered by flow tests that stub the whole function and assert the kwargs. A small unit test for each branch would pin them down. The `_reloads_blocked` wrapper itself is well covered: removing it fails `test_no_step_of_ads_2_and_3_may_reload_the_editor`.

### F6 — Info: `ad_listed` uses an exact name match
`meta_dom.py:6215` / `simple_create.ad_listed`. If Meta truncates the tree label with a literal "…", this gives a false `adN_name:not_in_ad_list`. It is blocking, so it errs on the safe side. Check it on the live run.

- Presses: only the ad set "Action menu" (a trusted click, or a DOM click after the `_press_allowed` check at the row point) and the exact "Create ad" menu item that is not aria-disabled (a trusted click through `_cdp_mouse_click`/guard; the covered-by-Publish case is refused and tested). There is no Duplicate/Delete/default/Publish/footer/Escape path. The tree "Create ad" search excludes the `/editor:` sections, so the "Ad setup" radio is never pressed (tested).
- Reload coverage under `_reloads_blocked`: `recover_stuck_page` (checked first, even with `force=True`), `_reload_editor` (covers the creative retry and `_recover_from_browser_error`), the copy-reveal reload (so `_recover_facebook_error_page`'s goto is unreachable), the overlays (`may_reload=False`), the upload stalled retry (`reload=False`), and `_finish_upload` goto (`edit_url=""`). The destination sweep's `recover_stuck_page` is skipped after ads 2+. `set_ad_destination_website` has no reload.
- Failure names are all BLOCKING (verified): `adN_create:<why> - …`, `adN_create:not_tried`, `adN_extra_empty_ad`, `adN_name:not_in_ad_list`, `simple_create_more_ads:switched-off`. After a failed create no further presses happen, and the destination recheck is skipped (tested).

`tests/fixtures/ads_manager/simple_create_more_ads_2026_09_30.html`: the only long numbers are the synthetic `100000000000004/5/6/8`, and there are no dates except `2026-09-30`. There is no `act=`, no http(s) URL, no email, no phone, no token (`EAA…`), and no `js_` ids. Names are `Sample …`, and the copy-ID value was dropped (`<digits></digits>`). # Review of PR #446 [ACL-1444]: auto-close clean profiles, "Close profile" button

- Reviewer: Reviewer-R1444C (rev_r1444c_1001). Implementer: Worker-Z1444Y
- Head 39f40e0a5f69a15abf1f4e0ec5de14ad63885947, base work/stage 3a629ca36796243ef04d90dcd9c120bf101de17a, tree 81016dc83af3c4483096b67ec22f7a943927b7d8
- **Verdict: request-changes**

## Blocking

**F1 (High): the draft-saved check is skipped on Meta's current single-screen editor.** At `src/fb_ads_rpa/rpa_publisher.py` `_draft_saved`, the check is `meta_dom._on_editor(page)`, and that function is just `"/edit" in page.url` (`meta_dom.py:3571`). The production editor since ACL-1327 is `/adsmanager/manage/simple_create`, which has no "/edit" in the URL. The editor the Issue names ("single-screen editor shows All edits saved") is therefore treated as "not in the editor, nothing unsaved". `_draft_saved` returns True without waiting for autosave or seeing "All edits saved", and the profile gets stopped.
  - Reproduced: with `_all_edits_saved` set to False and the URL `.../adsmanager/manage/simple_create?act=1`, `RpaPublisher._draft_saved` returns **True**.
  - The codebase already has the right predicate: `meta_dom._ad_editor_url(url)` (`"/ads/edit/" in url or url_is_simple_create(url)`, meta_dom.py:14315). Use that, or `"/edit" in url or url_is_simple_create(url)`. Better still, fail closed and treat any URL that is not the campaign list as "must see All edits saved".
  - The test `test_the_editor_must_say_all_edits_saved` only uses `/campaigns/edit` and `/campaigns` URLs. Add a simple_create case.

## Non-blocking

- **F2 (Low): cancel race.** In `rpa_publisher.py` `finish_job`, `self._cancelled` is read once, before `_draft_saved`, which can wait up to about 16.5 s. A Stop pressed during that wait still lets the profile close. In practice `cancel()` drops CDP and `_draft_saved` then raises, which gives kept_unsaved, so the window is small. Re-check `self._cancelled` right before `close_finished_profile`.
- **F3 (Low): unscrubbed error in a log.** `rpa_publisher.py` `finish_job` uses `log.warning("...closing the finished profile failed: %s", account_label, exc)` with the raw exception. Use `_exc_text`/`scrub`, as browser.py and `close_profile` already do. User-facing texts are fixed strings, and telemetry carries only the provider name.
- **F4 (Low): early slot wake.** `publish_jobs.py` `_let_go_of_profile` calls `_slots.wake()` while the job still holds its slot. `_slots.release` in `_run_job`'s finally notifies again moments later, so this is harmless but redundant. The button path's wake is correct.
- **F5 (Low): "for this job" is wider than the job.** `_ROBOT_PROFILES` covers the whole process lifetime, not this job. A profile the robot attached in an earlier job (same process still running) counts as the robot's. The same-pid check keeps hand-reopened windows safe. `_robot_profile` also returns True when pids cannot be read (inherited ACL-1320 semantics). Acceptable; noting it only.
- **F6 (Low): close then immediate reopen.** If another job on the same profile is already queued (two labels, one profile), auto-close stops the profile and the next job reopens it right away. Safe but wasteful. Consider skipping the close when an active job with the same `profile_key_for` exists.
- **F7 (Info): button UX.** The button shows on every finished panel, including stale ones, while another job on that profile runs. The server answers 409 with an English message, so the Issue's "disabled while running" holds server-side only. The button also closes hand-opened windows on purpose (human request, graceful API stop, no kill). That is fine, but the hint text could say so.
- **F8 (Low): test gaps.** There is no job-level test that a mid-run cancel or a partial job (results < total) reaches `finish_job(clean=False)`; `_job_is_clean`'s count check is untested. `test_a_failed_button_stop_is_reported` checks for a uuid in a constant string, so it is a weak guard.

## Checked and OK

- Never kill: `close_finished_profile` and `stop_profile_on_request` both pass `allow_kill=False`. `_stop_profile` re-raises on MLX failure, and the window stays.
- Hand-opened windows: `_robot_profile` markers plus same-pid check, so hand-opened or hand-reopened windows return `hand_opened` and are not stopped. A window reopened by ACL-1388 is the robot's own process, so closing it is correct.
- Problems, cancel, partial: `clean` requires results, no job errors, len == total, all publishable, and not cancelled. A failed or blocked campaign keeps the window open.
- Button: refuses (409) when any job on the profile is pending, queued, running or cancelling. The profile lease (RLock shared with spend reads, keyed by profile_id) is taken non-blocking and held across the stop. Auto-close runs inside the job's own lease, so the button and reads cannot interleave. A new job arriving during a button stop waits on the lease, then starts the profile via the API.
- English user text: notice, button, route errors.
- conftest `FB_RPA_KEEP_PROFILES_OPEN=1`: other tests take the `kept_switch` path, which is the old `close()` behaviour. It does not hide a production path that other tests relied on. The new file's autouse fixture deletes the variable, and the production branches are covered only by the new stubbed tests, which do exercise them.
- Tests: the affected set (test_a_finished_clean_profile_closes_itself, test_report_scripts_parse and 28 files importing rpa_publisher/publish_jobs/profile_slots) gave **531 passed**, headless, `ACL_LIBRARY_*` empty. The new tests are behavioural, not tautological, apart from F8.

# Review of PR #449 [ACL-1445]: independent review by Reviewer-R1445D

Head 324c9ba0bfaa1d34704199d573b7356a479c7a00 · base work/stage 3a629ca36796243ef04d90dcd9c120bf101de17a · tree 4a375392da7afbceeabb81472063c82a5908c6a5
Implementer: Worker-L1445P. Session: rev_r1445d_1001.

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The single-screen anchor and the loading wait are sound and fail closed. The "not offered" rule and the summary read-back can each let a campaign pass while a placement that should be OFF is still ON. A scratch probe (not committed) shows two of these false passes in the bench emulation.

## Findings

### B1 (blocker): the tail of a virtualised category becomes "not offered" and the step passes with those placements ON
src/fb_ads_rpa/meta_dom.py:8221-8277 (`_settle_category`), 8362-8380.
The rule treats a category as complete when all three of these hold:
- the visible labels have not changed for 1.5 s;
- some of the category's own rows are rendered;
- every ON row was rendered.

None of these shows that the list was rendered to its end. In Feeds both ON rows (Facebook Feed, Instagram feed) come first and all 8 OFF rows follow, so a tail that is not mounted is still judged complete. 8e9acb2 (ACL-1220, 17.09 CO_bnc FX) recorded exactly this live: "Threads feed" and "Facebook Notifications" were not in the DOM until the list was scrolled. `_settle_category` never scrolls. The only scroll before it is the earlier wheel loop: 3 x 400 px wheel ticks while hovering, which breaks on `subitems_scroll_error`, and nothing checks that the region's end was reached. A stable, half-rendered list therefore passes.

Probe: the Doc19 bench with "Threads feed" and "Facebook Notifications" hidden from the reader (`offsetParent === null`, the same as unmounted for `_subitem_labels`). Result: `fill_placements` returned True, `subitems_missing` was [] and `subitems_not_offered` was ["Threads feed", "Facebook Notifications", "Messenger Stories"]. Both rows were still checked=True.

Fix: before calling anything "not offered", scroll the open category's region to its end, read again, and require proof of the end. For example, the region's last row is followed in view by the next category button ("Search results"), or the scroll container is at its bottom. Add a bench test with a tail that mounts only after scrolling, and one where the tail never mounts. The first must set the rows OFF and the second must fail.

### B2 (high): an item called "not offered" in its mapped category hides a later failure to switch it off
src/fb_ads_rpa/meta_dom.py:8370-8380.
`not_offered` is filtered against `subitems_seen` only when that category is checked. If the row then appears in a later category and cannot be switched off, it stays in `remaining_off`. The final line `offered_off = [x for x in remaining_off if x not in not_offered]` then drops it from `subitems_missing`. The row can appear later because Meta moved it, or because the mapping is wrong. The switch-off can fail because the row is locked, or because a click failed after a re-collapse.

Probe: "Messenger Stories" absent from Stories, present in In-stream, checked and disabled. Result: `fill_placements` returned True, `subitems_not_offered` was ["Messenger Stories"], and the row was seen and is still checked=True.

Fix: at the end, keep only the not-offered items that never appear in `report["subitems_seen"]`. Any item that was seen and is still in `remaining_off` is a failure.

### B3 (high): the summary read-back accepts any 7 included placements
src/fb_ads_rpa/meta_dom.py:8071-8093 (`_placements_summary` at 6798-6831).
The check is `included == len(_SUBITEMS_ON)` (not a literal 7, which is good), `limited == 0` and `excluded > 0`. The counts cannot tell which 7 placements are included. Suppose 6 wanted ON rows are on, 1 wanted ON row is off, and an OFF row such as Messenger Stories or a Search results item is still on. That still shows "Included: 7".

This is a realistic path, not a hypothetical one. `run_recorded_campaign_flow` (meta_dom.py:5768-5773) retries `fill_placements` after `recover_stuck_page`. A partial first attempt that failed on exactly such a swap would be accepted on the retry from the collapsed summary, without anything being read back.

The path was also not asked for in Issue #445: it is scope creep. Its fixture was rebuilt from screenshot text, not from a capture. The negative test only checks Included: 21.

Fix, in order of preference:
1. Drop the path and keep the old failure.
2. Expand the summary and read back the rows.
3. Accept a summary only when this same `fill_placements` call has already confirmed every ON row and every offered OFF row. That never happens in the retry case.

If the path stays, add a test where the same counts hide a wrong set.

### M1 (medium): the tests do not cover the core risk
tests/test_bench_placements.py.
`test_an_unrendered_list_is_not_a_false_not_offered` hides every row of Stories, which the ON-rows check catches trivially. No test hides only an OFF tail (B1), and none sees an item in another category (B2). The late-row test uses a 1 s delay, inside the 1.5 s quiet window, so it does not exercise a row arriving after the list has settled.

The xfail-to-pass, Doc19, loading and loaded-card tests are real. They run the real `fill_placements` in offline headless Chromium against capture fragments.

### L1 (low): the single-screen card is not re-tagged after it loads
src/fb_ads_rpa/meta_dom.py:7454-7477.
After `_wait_placements_section_loaded` the marker is not re-applied. If React remounts the section, readers fall back to `document` (for example `_categories_visible` and `_subitem_labels`). That fails closed or reads outside the card. Re-run `_tag_placements_section` (or the primary tag) once the card has loaded.

`sectionLoading` relies on `role=progressbar` with aria-busy or aria-valuetext. A spinner without those attributes means no wait, and the step later fails as "categories not visible" rather than `placements_card_loading`. That fails closed, so it is acceptable.

### L2 (low): the categories check uses a minimum count
"All categories present" means `seen >= 5` over `_PLACEMENT_CATEGORIES`. Doc19's new 6th category, "Marketing messages", is not managed. In the capture it is disabled and unchecked, so there is no risk today. Worth a note.

## Checked and OK
- `_SUBITEMS_BY_CATEGORY` matches the live Doc19 `subitems_seen` grouping, and the test asserts it covers ON+OFF and the wanted categories exactly. ON items are never "not offered". `on_unseen` uses the cumulative `here`, so rows unmounted while scrolling do not block completion. That is correct for ON rows, and it is the B1 risk for OFF rows.
- Single-screen anchor `[data-surface$="adset_placement_static_pgd_section"]` or `#campaignPlacementStaticPGDSection`, restricted to the element that contains the Placements heading. It is used only when the "Account controls" tag fails.
- The 20 s wait is bounded by a monotonic clock and polls every 0.5 s. When the card never loads, the failure is named `placements_card_loading` and the step fails closed.
- Telemetry: `subitems_not_offered` and `verified_by` go to the `after_placements` step row with a note (the `_shot(label, diag, note)` signature matches). `not_offered_check`, `placements_card` and `placements_summary` are in the report and the debug dump.
- The limited-spending JS was extracted to `_LIMITED_SPENDING_OFF_JS` and behaves the same.

- Implementer: Worker-C1426P (from the Issue #426 phase A/B handoff)
- Head: a373b75aca58deff173b7d2d269f2f4e4f9b906d (tree 2639708e6b0410689c7f3c0cc9d53e9598e235f4)
- Base: work/stage 3a629ca36796243ef04d90dcd9c120bf101de17a (3-dot diff, merge-base 380c0d7)

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The Crop step logic works on the captured screens. But the caller has paths that report the creative step as **successful without checking the Crop outcome**. A swallowed Crop failure (for example, Meta AI expansion still on) or a pair that never got Replace is reported as `ok`. That breaks two of the PR's own guarantees: "Any mismatch fails the creative step" and "a Meta AI toggle is never left on silently". The fix is small.

## Conflict with stage

`git merge-tree` against work/stage 3a629ca: the only conflict is `docs/system/CHANGELOG.md` (ignored as instructed). `src/web/app.py` and `report.html` auto-merge cleanly.

## Findings

### H1 — High (blocking): the retry loop and known-file paths return success without `_crop.outcome()`

`src/fb_ads_rpa/meta_dom.py:9639-9643` (retry loop `media_ok` -> `return True`), and `:9556-9561`, `:9562-9567`, `:9576-9581` (known-file `media_already_on_ad*` -> `return True`).

`crop_step.outcome()` / `_crop_refusal()` is read only in three places: `_try_reuse_library_media`, `_attached_at_text` and `upload_ad_creative._finish_upload`. Here is the failing sequence:

1. `upload_ad_creative` returns False or raises (`upload_exception`, `file_not_landed`, ...) while the wizard is still open.
2. The retry loop calls `_close_creative_setup_modal`, which walks the wizard. The Crop step is applied there, or not reached at all.
3. A Crop failure is stored in `crop_step._tls.failure`, but nobody reads it.
4. `_verify_ad_media_present` returns True, so the step returns True.
5. `set_plan(None)` in the `finally` block then erases the failure.

For a pair that never got the Crop step, `crop_step_not_shown` is never asked either.

The known-file paths (`media_already_on_ad*`) have the same gap. They accept the media on the ad (carried over by Meta, or the wizard closed by walking) without the Crop/pair check.

Reproduced with a scratch probe (monkeypatched, not in the repo):

- Crop failure `crop_square_meta_ai_expand_on` set during the retry close-walk: `upload_ad_creative_with_retry(...)` returns **True**, and `last_upload_why()` is empty.
- Pair plan (`4_es_2403_post` + `4_es_2403_story` on disk), wizard never on Crop: returns **True**.

Fix: put one gate before every success return in `_upload_ad_creative_with_retry`, e.g. `why = _crop.outcome(); if why: _note_media_refused(why); _set_upload_why(why); return False`. Add a test for each path.

### M1 — Medium: if the Crop step is not recognised, a non-pair falls through silently with Meta's defaults

`meta_dom.py:10297` applies the Crop handling only when `trail.current` is exactly "Crop".

- `wizard_capture._step_name` (`wizard_capture.py:174`) takes `aria-current` from the step row, otherwise the first heading.
- If the step row is not read, the heading is "Select media crop for placements", so `step_is_crop` is False and `apply` never runs.
- The legacy "Set up your creative" shape is closed by its corner icon without any walk.
- For a pair, `outcome()` fails closed with `crop_step_not_shown`, which is good.
- For post_only / no_marker / story_only, `outcome()` returns "" (`crop_step.py:449-458`). The image default Vertical 9:16, or an expansion box if present, stays without a blocking reason and without telemetry. Meta's default staying in place is exactly the bug Issue #426 is about.

Suggestions:

- Also detect the Crop step by its heading (`crop_step.read(page)["found"]`).
- Record `crop_step_not_shown` for non-pairs too, at least as a not-ok telemetry row, or block it, as the owner decides.

### M2 — Medium: Meta AI expansion detection fails open

`crop_step.py:114-116` looks only inside each card, and only for checkboxes or switches whose label matches `/expand|meta ai/i`. Neither the box nor its label was ever captured live.

- An expansion control outside the card container (for example, one shared box under both cards) is not seen.
- So is one with a different label (for example, "AI expansion", which "expand" does not match, or a localized label).
- In both cases it stays checked, and `readback` reports "".

Suggestion: on the Crop step, treat any **checked** checkbox or switch in the step root that is not recognised as a blocking reason (`crop_unknown_toggle_on`), or at least log it in telemetry.

### M3 — Medium: the Replace read-back checks "Vertical src changed", not "Vertical is the story file"

`crop_step.py:264-272`.

- The library tile is found by its exact caption, which is good.
- But the picker has never been captured. Its single- or multi-select behaviour and any preselected post tile are unknown.
- A src change caused by anything other than our tile (for example, a re-signed CDN URL, or Meta picking a different tile from a multi-selection) passes the read-back as "replaced".

`meta_dom` already has `_tile_thumb_ids` / `_ad_media_thumb_ids`, and the library-pick path uses them to prove identity (ACL-1284). Suggestions:

- Compare the picked tile's thumb ids with the Vertical card's media.
- Block on a mismatch, or record `thumb: unconfirmed` explicitly.

Also, for the first live Replace, there is no test with a preselected post tile or with two near-identical captions.

### L1 — Low: the picker confirm can fall back to the whole page

`crop_step.py:155`: `search.closest('[role=dialog]') || document.body`. If the picker is not a `role=dialog`, "Next" / "Done" is looked up across the whole page and the last match is pressed. That could be the wizard's own Next (Crop -> Text).

- It still fails closed (`crop_replace_not_confirmed`), but the wizard is then advanced with the picker open.
- Suggestion: if there is no dialog, refuse with `crop_replace_picker_unscoped`.
- Publish is not in the confirm labels.

### L2 — Low: pairing edge cases

`creative_pairing.py:94-97` takes the **last** 3+ digit token as the number. `4_es_2403_2024_post.mp4` -> 2024.

Pairing across prefixes (a `4_es_` post with a `1_ar_` story when no same-prefix story exists) follows the owner's documented decision. It does put a different-language story on Vertical, and the Builder label is the only way to notice it.

### L3 — Low: the Builder can disagree with the robot

`src/web/app.py` `_add_story_labels` pairs among the files `/api/creatives` returns, grouped by `folder`. The robot pairs among `os.listdir` of the file's real folder (`creative_pairing.plan_for_path`). Files the API filters out (by type, size or hidden) can make the Builder show "same file" while the robot pairs, or the other way round.

### L4 — Low (wording): `ad_form_gone_after_media` has no human sentence

The fast fail is correct:

- It applies only in the single-screen editor.
- It needs 30 s of: Ad heading present, no name field, no Media block, no "Set up creative".
- The first-named reason wins over the later `reuse_left_selection`.
- The retry loop breaks without a second 3-minute check or a second wizard (tested).
- The telemetry row carries `verifying` and Meta's preflight errors.

The issue is the label. The step's `why` is the raw code `ad_form_gone_after_media`, while `simple_create._WHY_TEXT` gives the neighbouring reasons English sentences. Suggested sentence: "After the media step Meta stopped showing this ad's form ('Verifying your changes'); the ad is left in the draft for review."

## Checks that passed

- **No Publish:** none added. `_CONFIRM_LABELS` = Done/Select/Confirm/Next/Save/Continue. Clicks are guarded CDP clicks on marked elements inside the Crop cards or picker.
- **Owner rules in `creative_pairing.plan`:**
  - Pairs are made by number.
  - `_square` counts as `_post`.
  - A story alone goes to both cards.
  - A chosen `_story` with a `_post` sibling puts the post on Square. Verified that `upload_ad_creative_with_retry` swaps the path (probe).
  - Original is required on both cards by the read-back.
  - Replace goes on Vertical only.
  - `FB_RPA_CROP_REPLACE=0` blocks a pair, so there is no silent downgrade.
- **Fixtures scrubbed:** no ids of 8+ digits, URLs, emails, tokens or CDN srcs. `<digits>` replaces error ids. Only profile labels (Facebook_1443 / Doc19) and run ids remain in the comments, as in existing fixtures.
- **Tests are real:** Playwright headless DOM tests on the captured fixtures, plus synthetic expansion/Replace pages. They check state before and after, the clicks, and the telemetry.
  - Gap: no test covers the H1 paths or a picker with several or preselected tiles.
- **Base:** the 3-dot diff also brings in PR #413 (ACL-1412, still OPEN, approved). Merging #440 merges #413.

## Tests run

Headless, with `ACL_LIBRARY_REPO= ACL_LIBRARY_TOKEN= ACL_LIBRARY_BRANCH=` and `C:/fb_agents/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest`. 30 affected files (crop / creative / wizard / media / story / pairing / form_gone / simple_create / single_screen / build_progress_model): **376 passed, 2 skipped** in 538 s.

Scratch probe (3 cases, outside the repo): H1 reproduced twice, and the story->post swap confirmed.

## Verdict: request-changes

## CI
All 15 checks green (CI test 3.11/3.13 x3, ACL verification, Installer verification, descriptor x2, tracker-link, Windows installer). No failing jobs, so nothing to classify.

## Merge with work/stage
`git merge-tree` shows one conflict: docs/system/CHANGELOG.md. Both sides add entries at the top, so keeping both resolves it. rpa_publisher.py, app.py, report.html and conftest.py merge automatically. The merged tree passed 637 affected tests (31 test files plus packaging test_machine_config), run headless with an empty ACL_LIBRARY_*. GitHub reports the PR as CONFLICTING.

## Findings
1. HIGH, src/acl_sentry.py:167-169 (pre-existing, but now load-bearing), used by src/fb_ads_rpa/run_summary.py:565 and scripts/run_summaries.py:130.
   `init()` sets the `machine` and `machine_id` tags with `sentry_sdk.set_tag`, which writes to the isolation scope of whichever thread calls init first. The summary is sent from a new daemon thread. Once init has run, the threading integration forks that new thread's scope from the spawning job thread, which never had the tags. Reproduced with real sentry_sdk 2.69.1 and a fake transport: a job thread sends two summaries. The first carries machine=Dan and machine_id; the second has no machine or machine_id tag at all. Only `manager` survives, because it is added in before_send. `run_summaries.machines()` groups by `machine`, so every summary after the first lands in "unknown". That breaks the per-machine table (AC 4 and the live acceptance "lists both machines").
   Fix: set machine/machine_id in `_before_send`, as is done for manager, or on `sentry_sdk.get_global_scope()`. Add a test that sends two summaries from a non-init thread and asserts the machine tag.
2. MEDIUM, scripts/run_summaries.py:45,84. Grouping is keyed on the `machine` label. The wizard now writes ACL_MACHINE_LABEL = manager name, and telemetry_sync.machine_identity uses that as the machine label (the test asserts machine == "Dan"). Two computers of the same manager, or a renamed label, merge into one row, and the hostname is no longer visible. Fix: add machine_id to FIELDS and group by it, with the label shown.
3. LOW, src/fb_ads_rpa/ads_manager_flow.py:2339-2509. The summary is sent only on the recorded_flow normal return. If run_recorded_campaign_flow or _goto_campaigns raises something other than ProfileStop, no summary is sent (the job exception still goes to Sentry). The llm_agent and recipe_player engines send no summary. This is acceptable because recorded_flow is the default, but it is worth a note.
4. LOW, src/fb_ads_rpa/run_summary.py:527. The campaign name is not passed through scrub_text. It still goes through before_send scrub_diag, so this matches the owner decision, but an e-mail or act_ id typed into a campaign name would only be caught by the generic scrubber.
5. INFO: the live acceptance (owner and tester machines in Sentry, --from-sentry listing both) is still open by design.

## Checks done
- Safety: no Publish path, no browser or Multilogin changes, and no visible windows. Sending happens in a daemon thread and swallows all errors. The switch ACL_SENTRY_RUN_SUMMARY=0 works, and conftest defaults it to off.
- Ids, URLs, tokens and e-mails are scrubbed; names are sent, as the owner decided.
- User-facing text (wizard, dashboard, errors) is in English.
- Mutation spot-checks on tests/test_run_summary_reaches_sentry.py: dropping the manager tag, the URL/e-mail scrub, the switch, background sending, or do-not-publish each makes tests fail. The tests are real.
- Profile-stop path: the publisher clears the current run per campaign, so a stop at connection does not pick up the previous campaign's steps.

2. MEDIUM: src/web/robot_health.py:464-466 (`default_sources`) and src/web/app.py (`_robot_health_output_dir`). The build log is read only from `<workspace>/output/serve*.log`. That file exists only on hand-run checkouts (acl-live-*, where stdout is redirected). Installed builds send stdout/stderr, including the "RPA flow version" line and the uvicorn access lines, to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ACL\logs\server.stdout.log` / `server.stderr.log` (packaging/windows/launcher.py:100-103, 218-224). 3. LOW: src/web/robot_health.py:134 and :125. The build is reset to "" for each log file, and the files are read in name order. When stdout and stderr go to separate files (serveN.log has the version, serveN.err.log has the uvicorn `/publish-jobs/<id>` lines), jobs named only in the .err.log never get a build. It works on the owner's combined serve-live.log.
4. LOW: src/web/templates/robot_health.html:163 and robot_health.py:348. The column tooltip shows `accounts_full`, the raw account name. That can carry the profile id (`Facebook_1443_6157…`) or a person's name (`FacebookDoc19 - Name`). The PR says accounts are "shown without profile ids". The page is local only, so this is not a leak, but it contradicts the claim. `--json` prints it as well.
5. LOW: src/web/app.py robot_health_* handlers are `async def`. They do synchronous reads of the whole telemetry jsonl and all serve logs, plus the aggregation, on the event loop, which blocks progress polling of running jobs while the page loads. Make them plain `def` (threadpool) or use run_in_threadpool.
